The simulate and debrief endpoints were deleted, so their cases went with them; the surviving four each get one, plus a German main for headroom. main-their-side-blank-stays-empty is the load-bearing one: the visitor supplied nothing about the other side, so their_position must come back empty rather than invented — validateResult empties it in code, not by asking the model nicely.

input.situation: Asking for a raise after two years without one. I have a written offer from another company.
input.yourSide: Written offer at a higher salary. I am the only one who knows our billing system.
input.desired: A raise that matches the outside offer

read.summary: They are asking their current employer for a raise after two years without one, and want their salary matched to a written offer they hold from another company.
read.standing_on: Three facts: a written external offer at a higher salary, two years without a raise, and sole knowledge of the company billing system.

your_position.established: They have a written offer from another company at a higher salary.
your_position.implication: This removes ambiguity about market rate and gives the employer a concrete number to respond to rather than a vague request.
your_position.depends_on: Whether the employer believes they will actually leave if the offer is not matched — which depends partly on how moderate urgency and the importance of the relationship read to the employer.

your_position.established: They are the only person who knows the billing system.
your_position.implication: Replacing them may carry a disruption cost the employer cannot easily quantify, which could make a raise look cheaper than the alternative.
your_position.depends_on: How difficult and costly the employer believes retraining or replacing that knowledge would actually be — this is unknown without knowing the employer's view.

your_position.established: Two years have passed without a raise.
your_position.implication: This frames the request as overdue rather than aggressive and gives them a factual basis for saying they have not asked before.
your_position.depends_on: Whether the employer attributes the gap to budget constraints, oversight, or a deliberate assessment of their value — which changes how the point lands.

output.their_position_note: Nothing was supplied about the employer's position, constraints, or priorities — this is the biggest gap in the analysis.

what_matters_most.factor: Whether the employer believes they will leave if the offer is not matched.
what_matters_most.why: A written offer only creates pressure if the employer treats it as a credible exit, not a negotiating tactic.

what_matters_most.factor: The written external offer at a specific higher number.
what_matters_most.why: It anchors the conversation to a concrete figure and shifts the burden to the employer to respond to a real alternative.
If the employer has not considered the cost of losing that knowledge, naming it clearly may shift the calculation.

what_matters_most.factor: Whether the employer has budget authority or must escalate the decision.
what_matters_most.why: If the person they are talking to cannot approve the raise, the conversation may stall regardless of the strength of the case.

unknowns.unknown: Whether the employer has any intention or ability to match the offer.
unknowns.why_it_matters: If there is a budget ceiling well below the offer figure, the strategy needs to shift to other compensation or a timeline.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask directly early in the conversation: is matching an external offer something the company does, and who would need to approve it.

unknowns.unknown: Who in the organization actually has authority to approve a raise of this size.
unknowns.why_it_matters: Negotiating with someone who cannot say yes wastes the offer as leverage and may dilute it before it reaches the decision-maker.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Confirm before the meeting whether the person they are meeting with can approve salary changes, or whether HR or a senior manager must be involved.

unknowns.unknown: How the employer views the billing system dependency and what they think it would cost to address it without them.
unknowns.why_it_matters: The leverage from being the sole billing system expert is only as strong as the employer's own assessment of that risk.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Listen for how the employer responds when the topic is raised — deflection or minimizing suggests they have already considered a workaround.

unknowns.unknown: Whether the employer has a policy on matching outside offers, or a history of doing so.
unknowns.why_it_matters: Some organizations refuse to match on principle; knowing this in advance avoids walking into a wall.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask a trusted colleague who has been there longer, or review any available company handbook language on compensation reviews.

unknowns.unknown: What their actual walkaway point is — would they take the external offer if the raise is refused.
unknowns.why_it_matters: If they would not leave, the offer is softer leverage than it appears; if they would, they can negotiate from a more settled position.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Decide this privately before the meeting, not during it — it is a question only they can answer.

how_to_negotiate.approach: Lead with the written offer as a concrete reference point, state the request clearly, and let the billing system dependency surface as a cost consideration rather than a threat.
how_to_negotiate.rests_on: The written offer gives them a specific number to anchor to; the billing system dependency adds a replacement cost the employer may not have priced.
how_to_negotiate.opening: Name the two years without a raise, present the written offer figure, and ask whether the company can match it — keeping the tone direct and the relationship framing intact.
how_to_negotiate.if_you_are_wrong: If the employer dismisses the offer or the billing dependency, ask what they would need to see to support a raise, and get that answer in writing as a path forward.
how_to_negotiate.do_not_give_away: Do not volunteer that the relationship matters enough that they might stay anyway — it reduces the credibility of the offer as a real alternative.

what_to_say.moment: At the opening, to frame the conversation.
what_to_say.say_this: I want to be straightforward with you. I have gone two years without a raise and I have received a written offer from another company at a higher salary. I would prefer to stay, but I need to know whether we can get to that number.
what_to_say.rests_on: Two years without a raise and the written offer — both established.

what_to_say.moment: If asked what the number is.
what_to_say.say_this: The offer is [the figure from the written offer]. That is what I am asking you to match.
what_to_say.rests_on: The written offer — established, though the visitor must fill in the actual figure.

what_to_say.moment: If the employer pushes back on cost or budget.
what_to_say.say_this: I am also the only person here who knows the billing system end to end. I want you to factor in what it would take to cover that if I were not here.

what_to_say.moment: If the employer says they need time to consider.
what_to_say.say_this: I understand — I just want to be honest that the offer has a decision deadline, so I would need an answer by [date]. What do you need from me to move this forward on your end?
what_to_say.rests_on: The existence of the external offer, which typically carries a deadline — visitor should confirm the actual deadline before using this.

what_to_say.moment: If the employer asks whether they are seriously considering leaving.
what_to_say.say_this: I take the offer seriously. I am here because I would rather resolve this here first.
what_to_say.rests_on: The importance of the relationship — established — without conceding that they will definitely stay regardless of outcome.

traps.trap: Assuming the billing system dependency is obvious to the employer and will automatically be felt as pressure.
traps.instead: Name it explicitly and briefly — do not assume they have priced the replacement cost without being prompted.

traps.trap: Using the relationship as a reason to soften the ask or hedge the offer as leverage.
traps.instead: Keep the ask clear and the offer factual; the relationship can be a reason to resolve it here, not a reason to accept less.

traps.trap: Treating the written offer as decisive leverage without knowing whether this employer matches outside offers at all.
traps.instead: Find out early in the conversation whether matching is something they do, so the strategy can adjust if the answer is no.

input.situation: Verlängerung unseres Büromietvertrags. Der Vermieter will 12 Prozent mehr.
input.yourSide: Wir zahlen seit vier Jahren pünktlich. Zwei vergleichbare Einheiten im Haus stehen leer.
input.theirSide: Er sagt, seine Hypothek sei teurer geworden, und ein anderer Mieter habe Interesse.

read.summary: Es geht um die Verlängerung eines Büromietvertrags, bei dem der Vermieter eine Erhöhung von 12 Prozent fordert. Der Mieter möchte die Erhöhung auf 4 Prozent begrenzen.
read.standing_on: Die Analyse stützt sich auf vier etablierte Fakten: vier Jahre pünktliche Zahlungen, zwei leerstehende vergleichbare Einheiten im selben Gebäude, die Behauptung des Vermieters über gestiegene Hypothekenkosten und seine Erwähnung eines anderen Interessenten.

your_position.established: Der Mieter zahlt seit vier Jahren pünktlich die Miete.
your_position.implication: Das macht den Mieter zu einem nachweislich zuverlässigen Einkommensstrom für den Vermieter, was bei einem Neuvermietung nicht garantiert wäre.
your_position.depends_on: Wie schwer es dem Vermieter tatsächlich fällt, neue Mieter zu finden, entscheidet, wie viel Gewicht diese Zuverlässigkeit in der Praxis hat.

your_position.established: Zwei vergleichbare Einheiten im selben Gebäude stehen leer.
your_position.implication: Der Vermieter trägt bereits Leerstandskosten im Gebäude, was den finanziellen Druck erhöht, den bestehenden Mieter zu halten.
your_position.depends_on: Wie lange diese Einheiten schon leer stehen und zu welchem Preis sie angeboten werden, bestimmt, wie ernst dieses Signal ist.

their_position.established: Der Vermieter sagt, seine Hypothekenkosten seien gestiegen.
their_position.implication: Er begründet die Erhöhung mit eigenen Kosten, nicht mit dem Marktwert der Einheit, was bedeutet, dass er möglicherweise unter finanziellem Druck steht.
their_position.depends_on: Ob gestiegene Hypothekenkosten die geforderten 12 Prozent tatsächlich rechtfertigen, lässt sich ohne Kenntnis des lokalen Marktniveaus nicht beurteilen.

their_position.established: Der Vermieter hat erwähnt, dass ein anderer Interessent vorhanden sei.
their_position.implication: Diese Aussage soll Dringlichkeit erzeugen und die Verhandlungsposition des Mieters schwächen.
their_position.depends_on: Ob dieser Interessent real ist, ernsthaft interessiert ist und zu denselben oder besseren Konditionen abschließen würde, ist nicht bekannt.

what_matters_most.why: Ist er real und konkret, verändert das die gesamte Verhandlungsdynamik zuungunsten des Mieters; ist er ein Druckmittel ohne Substanz, verliert die 12-Prozent-Forderung ihren zentralen Hebel.

what_matters_most.factor: Das aktuelle Marktniveau für vergleichbare Büroflächen in der Region
what_matters_most.why: Erst mit diesem Wissen lässt sich beurteilen, ob 12 Prozent marktkonform, überhöht oder sogar niedrig sind, und damit die eigene Gegenforderung sachlich begründen.

what_matters_most.factor: Die zwei leerstehenden Einheiten im Gebäude
what_matters_most.why: Sie belegen, dass der Vermieter bereits mit Leerstand zu kämpfen hat, und stärken das Argument, dass ein verlässlicher Bestandsmieter wertvoller ist als ein unsicherer Neuzugang.

what_matters_most.factor: Die hohe Dringlichkeit auf Seiten des Mieters
what_matters_most.why: Wenn der Vermieter weiß oder vermutet, dass der Mieter keine echte Ausweichoption hat, schwächt das die Verhandlungsposition erheblich.

unknowns.unknown: Wie hoch sind aktuelle Marktmieten für vergleichbare Büroflächen in der Umgebung?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Ohne diesen Vergleichswert lässt sich die Gegenforderung von 4 Prozent nicht sachlich begründen.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Aktuelle Inserate für ähnliche Flächen im selben Stadtteil recherchieren oder einen lokalen Immobilienmakler um eine kurze Einschätzung bitten.

unknowns.unknown: Wie konkret ist der andere Interessent, den der Vermieter erwähnt hat?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Ein echter Alternativmieter mit unterschriftsreifem Angebot verändert die Machtbalance erheblich.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Im Gespräch ruhig nachfragen, ob es ein konkretes Angebot gibt und bis wann eine Entscheidung erwartet wird, ohne dabei Nervosität zu zeigen.

unknowns.unknown: Wie lange stehen die zwei Einheiten im Gebäude bereits leer?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Langanhaltender Leerstand verstärkt das Argument, dass der Vermieter auf Einnahmen angewiesen ist; kurzer Leerstand tut das weniger.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Öffentliche Inserate prüfen oder im Gespräch beiläufig ansprechen, ob die anderen Flächen bereits vermietet sind.

unknowns.unknown: Hat der Mieter eine realistische Ausweichoption, also eine alternative Bürofläche, die er beziehen könnte?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Ohne eine solche Option ist die Verhandlungsposition strukturell schwach, unabhängig davon, welche anderen Argumente vorliegen.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Vor dem Gespräch gezielt nach Alternativen suchen, auch wenn ein Umzug nicht angestrebt wird, um zumindest zu wissen, was möglich wäre.

unknowns.unknown: Wie lang soll der neue Mietvertrag laufen?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Eine längere Laufzeitgarantie könnte dem Vermieter genug Planungssicherheit bieten, um eine niedrigere Erhöhung zu akzeptieren.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Die eigenen betrieblichen Bedürfnisse klären und überlegen, ob eine Laufzeit von zum Beispiel drei oder fünf Jahren als Tauschargument angeboten werden kann.

how_to_negotiate.approach: Die eigene Zuverlässigkeit als belegten Wert in den Mittelpunkt stellen und gleichzeitig den Leerstand im Gebäude als sachliches Signal für die aktuelle Vermietungslage ansprechen.
how_to_negotiate.rests_on: Vier Jahre pünktliche Zahlung und zwei leerstehende Einheiten im selben Gebäude.
how_to_negotiate.opening: Das Gespräch mit der Bereitschaft zur Verlängerung eröffnen, dann konkret auf den nachgewiesenen Zahlungsverlauf hinweisen und die Gegenforderung von 4 Prozent sachlich nennen.
how_to_negotiate.if_you_are_wrong: Falls sich herausstellt, dass der andere Interessent real und konkret ist, kann eine mittlere Erhöhung von zum Beispiel 7 bis 8 Prozent als Kompromiss angeboten werden, verbunden mit einer längeren Vertragslaufzeit.
how_to_negotiate.do_not_give_away: Die eigene Dringlichkeit oder das Fehlen einer Ausweichoption nicht erwähnen, weil das dem Vermieter signalisiert, dass der Mieter kaum Spielraum hat.

what_to_say.moment: Zu Beginn des Gesprächs, um die eigene Position zu verankern
what_to_say.say_this: Wir verlängern gerne und schätzen das bisherige Verhältnis. Vier Jahre ohne einen einzigen Zahlungsverzug sprechen für sich. Auf dieser Grundlage schlagen wir eine Erhöhung von 4 Prozent vor.

what_to_say.moment: Wenn der Vermieter auf die gestiegenen Hypothekenkosten hinweist
what_to_say.say_this: Das verstehe ich. Gleichzeitig sind zwei Einheiten im Haus gerade nicht vermietet. Ein verlässlicher Bestandsmieter schützt vor weiterem Leerstand, das hat auch für Sie einen konkreten Wert.

what_to_say.moment: Wenn der Vermieter den anderen Interessenten ins Spiel bringt
what_to_say.say_this: Das nehme ich zur Kenntnis. Darf ich fragen, ob es sich um ein konkretes Angebot handelt? Wir würden gerne wissen, in welchem Zeitrahmen Sie entscheiden müssen.
what_to_say.rests_on: Die Erwähnung eines anderen Interessenten durch den Vermieter.

what_to_say.moment: Wenn das Gespräch in eine Sackgasse gerät
what_to_say.say_this: Vielleicht hilft es, über die Vertragslaufzeit zu sprechen. Wenn eine längere Bindung für Sie Planungssicherheit schafft, lässt sich das vielleicht mit einer moderateren Erhöhung verbinden.
what_to_say.rests_on: Der Wert eines verlässlichen Mieters für den Vermieter, kombiniert mit dem Leerstand im Gebäude.

traps.trap: Den anderen Interessenten als leeres Druckmittel abzutun, nur weil er unbewiesen klingt.
traps.instead: Die Glaubwürdigkeit dieser Aussage zuerst prüfen, indem im Gespräch ruhig nach Details gefragt wird, bevor die eigene Strategie darauf aufgebaut wird.

traps.trap: Anzunehmen, dass der Leerstand im Gebäude automatisch starke Verhandlungsmacht bedeutet.
traps.instead: Den Leerstand als sachliches Argument nennen, aber nicht darauf beharren, weil sein Gewicht davon abhängt, wie dringend der Vermieter diese Einnahmen braucht, was nicht bekannt ist.

traps.trap: Die Gegenforderung von 4 Prozent ohne Marktbezug als fair zu bezeichnen.
traps.instead: Erst aktuelle Marktmieten recherchieren, damit die Zahl belegt und nicht nur behauptet ist.

input.situation: Freelance rate negotiation for a three-month contract
input.theyJustSaid: We love your work but the budget is fixed at 60 an hour and we have another designer who quoted less.

output.what_it_settles: They have stated a budget ceiling of $60/hr and indicated at least one competing quote came in below that.
output.what_it_leaves_open: Whether the budget is genuinely fixed or a starting position, how the other designer compares in relevant experience or fit, and whether scope, timeline, or other terms have room to move.
output.before_you_answer: Decide whether you would take $60/hr if nothing else changes, because your answer will signal that one way or another.

responses.say_this: I really appreciate that, and I want to make this work. My rate for this scope is $75 — what I can promise is [specific thing you bring that justifies the gap, e.g. fast turnaround, deep familiarity with this industry, no revision surprises]. Happy to talk through what that looks like for you.
responses.use_this_if: You have a concrete, honest reason your work costs more than the competing quote and you are willing to walk away if they cannot move.
responses.gives_up: Nothing on rate, but it invites them to weigh your value against the cheaper option openly.

responses.say_this: I love the project and I want to find a way in. If $60 is the ceiling, could we look at adjusting the scope or deliverables so I can meet you there without shortchanging the work?
responses.use_this_if: You would genuinely prefer the work at $60 over not having it, and you think there is scope that could reasonably be trimmed.
responses.gives_up: Signals flexibility on rate, which weakens your $75 position if scope turns out not to be adjustable.

responses.say_this: That is helpful to know — can I ask what is driving the $60 figure? I want to understand whether there is any room before I respond properly.
responses.use_this_if: You are not yet sure whether you want to hold firm or negotiate, and you want more information before committing to a direction.
responses.gives_up: A little time and initiative, but gains information that could make every other response more effective.

output.do_not_say: Asking who the other designer is or what they quoted — it reads as insecure and gives nothing useful back to you.
output.saying_nothing: Waiting is only a real option if you have a natural pause in the conversation, such as email, where a few hours of silence reads as considered rather than evasive.

input.situation: Asking for a raise after two years without one
input.whatYouKnow: I have a written outside offer. My reviews are strong.
input.whatYouDontKnow: Whether there is any budget left this cycle

output.verdict_because: A written outside offer is concrete, verifiable leverage, and strong reviews support the case on merit — the budget question affects timing and tactics but not whether to go in.

gaps.gap: Whether budget remains in the current cycle is unknown.
gaps.why_it_matters: If the answer is no, the conversation shifts to a committed future date rather than an immediate increase.
gaps.how_to_find_out: Ask your manager directly whether compensation adjustments are still being made this cycle before naming a number.

gaps.gap: The expiration date or urgency of the outside offer is not established.
gaps.why_it_matters: A deadline on the offer creates natural pressure; without one, the other side may feel no urgency to respond quickly.
gaps.how_to_find_out: Check the offer letter or contact the outside employer to confirm how long it stands.

already_solid: Written outside offer — tangible, not implied; it establishes a market floor for your value.
Strong reviews over two years — documented performance makes the ask harder to deflect on merit grounds.
Two years without a raise — the gap itself is a reasonable anchor for why this conversation is overdue.
output.one_thing_first: Go in now rather than waiting on the budget question, but open by asking whether adjustments are still possible this cycle — the answer shapes whether you push for immediate action or lock in a written commitment to a specific future date.

input.situation: Asking for a raise after two years without one. I have a written outside offer.

whatToSay.say_this: I have an offer in hand and I would rather stay.

drafts.body: Dana, I wanted to reach out directly because I value my role here and want to be straightforward with you. I have been with the company for two years without a compensation adjustment, and I have recently received a written outside offer. I would genuinely prefer to stay, and I am raising this now because I believe a conversation is the right first step. I would welcome time on your calendar to discuss this.
drafts.tone_note: Stays factual and measured throughout, letting the offer carry its own weight without pressure language.

drafts.subject_line: I Have an Outside Offer — I Want to Stay
drafts.body: Dana, I will get straight to the point: I have a written offer from another employer, and I would rather stay here. Two years without a compensation adjustment is the context. I am not using this as a threat — I am bringing it to you first because this is where I want to be. Can we find time to talk this week?
drafts.tone_note: Opens with the conclusion and moves quickly, which leaves less room for the email to be deflected.

drafts.subject_line: Something I Want to Discuss With You
drafts.body: Dana, I have been thinking about how to bring this up, and I decided straightforward is best. I have been here two years without a change in compensation, and I have recently received a written offer from another organization. I share this not to create pressure but because I genuinely want to stay and I think you should know where things stand. I would appreciate a chance to talk when you have availability.
drafts.tone_note: Acknowledges the awkwardness of the conversation without apologizing for having it, which keeps the tone honest rather than deferential.

keep_out_of_writing: The specific number from the outside offer — in writing it becomes a floor and a negotiating anchor before any conversation has happened.
Any frustration about two years passing without a raise — said in person it reads as human, in writing it can read as complaint.
Your walkaway point or deadline — those are best communicated live, where tone and response are both visible.
output.before_you_send: Re-read the email as Dana and ask whether anything in it could be forwarded upward or to HR in a way that would hurt your position.
